import pandas as pd

# Step 1: Load all source tables involved in the UNION operation
union_sources = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_9.csv"
]

# Read and concatenate all UNION source tables
union_dfs = []
for path in union_sources:
    df = pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure column '0' is integer type as per target schema
    df['0'] = df['0'].astype(int)
    union_dfs.append(df)

union_df = pd.concat(union_dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 2: Load the two source tables involved in the JOIN operation
# Source9_37_7 and Source9_37_10
df_7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
df_10 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/training_10.csv", index_col=0)

# Convert column '0' to int for consistency
df_7['0'] = df_7['0'].astype(int)
df_10['0'] = df_10['0'].astype(int)

# The JOIN operation is specified as JOIN : [["Source9_37_7", "Source9_37_10"], ["0", "0"]]
# Join on column '0' (inner join)
join_df = pd.merge(df_7, df_10, on='0', how='inner', suffixes=('_7', '_10'))

# After join, the schema will have columns: '0', '0_7', '0_10' but both original columns are named '0'
# Actually both columns are named '0' originally, so after merge we have only one '0' column plus any other columns.
# But both source tables have only column '0', so the join will produce columns: '0' only (no suffixes needed)
# But since both have only column '0', the join will produce just one column '0' (the join key).
# So join_df will have only column '0' (the join key).
# But since both tables have only column '0', the join is effectively intersection on '0'.

# Step 3: UNION the result of the JOIN with the previous UNION result
# Both union_df and join_df have column '0' only, so we can concat them

final_df = pd.concat([union_df, join_df], ignore_index=True)

# Step 4: Ensure the final dataframe matches the target schema and type
# Target schema: ['0': integer]
final_df['0'] = final_df['0'].astype(int)

# Step 5: Write the final dataframe to the target path
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_37/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
